subject: Template SLA: uptime banding and monthly credit proposal (OzoneTech)
messages:
From: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@ozonetech.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@ozonetech.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template ask — uptime floor and monthly remedy cap

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for last week’s briefing. We’ve reviewed the standard Redwood SLA and have a few asks that are blockers for procurement at OzoneTech. High level: we need an adjusted uptime baseline and a change to the monthly credit cap to satisfy our internal risk model.

Specifically:
- Target baseline: 99.5% (we understand Redwood’s standard is 99.9% — we’re proposing 99.5% as the committed floor for our account, with a defined remedy schedule).
- Monthly remedy cap: our CFO requires that monthly credits be capped at no more than 10% of monthly committed spend (the standard cap in our contracts).
- Maintenance carveouts: we need explicit regional maintenance windows and a notice window of 72 hours for non-emergency maintenance.

I’ve attached our procurement redlines and our SOC2 snapshot for your review. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 99.5% floor in the contract and how the credit ladder would look if the cap is constrained to 10%? We’re conscious of not wanting to erode your operational economics, but this is the gating item for our legal and procurement teams.

Attachments: ozonetech-desired-sla-redlines.docx, ozonetech_soc2_q1_2027.pdf

Thanks,
Elaine Torres
Head of Procurement, OzoneTech
elaine.torres@ozonetech.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@ozonetech.com>, OzoneTech Procurement <procurement@ozonetech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template ask — uptime floor and monthly remedy cap

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We’ve reviewed the request with Product and Finance and I wanted to outline a pragmatic counterproposal that balances OzoneTech’s risk constraints with Redwood’s service economics.

Quick answers up front:
- Baseline: We can offer a contractual floor of 99.8% for the first 12 months as a phased compromise (vs our standard 99.9%). After 12 months the floor would revert to standard terms unless we agree otherwise.
- Monthly credit cap: We can accept a 10% monthly cap on credits but we’ll need to adjust the credit ladder to preserve incentives — we propose a graduated ladder with smaller per-band payouts and a single "extraordinary incident" clause that allows limited exceedance subject to investigation and remedial plan.
- Maintenance: 72-hour notice for planned maintenance is acceptable for standard maintenance; critical security or emergency patches retain a shorter timeframe with post-event notice.

Proposed credit ladder (high level):
- 99.8%–100.0%: no credit
- 99.0%–99.79%: 5% credit of monthly committed spend per band
- 97.0%–98.99%: 10% credit of monthly committed spend per band
- <97.0%: 25% credit of monthly committed spend, subject to cap

With the 10% monthly cap in place, payout for multi-band losses would be prorated up to the 10% cap. For the first quarter we can offer a one-time onboarding credit of $10k to offset migration risk and accelerate acceptance.

I’ve uploaded a redline with these terms here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Ozone-SLA-Redlines (file: redwood-counterproposal-sla-redline.docx). Can you confirm whether a 99.8% phased floor meets procurement’s minimum? If not, we can escalate to execs for a 99.5 discussion but would need SVP approval.

Next steps suggestion:
1) OzoneTech confirm whether 99.8% phased floor is acceptable.
2) If yes, procurement signs off and we exchange a DocuSign for the SLA exhibit.
3) If no, we schedule a 30-min executive call to consider a 99.5% permanent floor and any offsetting commercial terms.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (503) 555-0122

[Attachment referenced: redwood-counterproposal-sla-redline.docx]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: OzoneTech ask — revenue / risk check

Marissa — quick internal note before we reply to Elaine formally.

Finance flagged that a permanent 99.5% contractual floor materially increases expected credit exposure over a 12‑month term, especially given OzoneTech’s bursty usage profile (their forecasted peak Q4 load is 3.5x baseline). Approving 99.8% phased floor plus the $10k onboarding credit keeps the modeled monthly exposure within tolerable limits for our FY27 plan.

If procurement insists on a permanent 99.5% floor we will need to offset with either:
- higher minimum committed spend, or
- an annualized cap (i.e., 10% monthly cap with an additional annual aggregate cap), or
- shorten opening maintenance notice to protect availability (not preferred).

Legal — Laura, are you comfortable with the extraordinary incident carveout language in the counterproposal redline? If so Marissa can push the current counter and reserve exec escalation if needed.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Torres <elaine.torres@ozonetech.com>, OzoneTech Procurement <procurement@ozonetech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood counterproposal — phased uptime floor, credit ladder, and onboarding credit

Elaine — following up with a formal counterproposal based on internal review. I’ve summarized the agreed changes and included the redline for signature. Please see the concrete terms below and the action items at the end.

Counterproposal summary:
- Phased uptime floor: 99.8% contractual floor for 12 months; after 12 months terms revert to Redwood standard (99.9%) unless parties agree in writing.
- Credit ladder (monthly):
  * 99.8%–100.0%: 0% credit
  * 99.0%–99.79%: 5% credit of monthly committed spend (per band)
  * 97.0%–98.99%: 10% credit of monthly committed spend (per band)
  * <97.0%: 25% credit of monthly committed spend, subject to the monthly cap
- Monthly credit cap: 10% of monthly committed spend. Multi-band incidents prorated up to the cap.
- Extraordinary incident clause: potential additional remediation subject to joint post‑incident review and exec approval; not automatic beyond the cap.
- Maintenance windows: 72 hours notice for planned maintenance; emergency patches treated as exception with post-event notice and RCA.
- One-time onboarding credit: $10,000 applied to first invoice after go‑live.

Next steps / action items:
1) If OzoneTech accepts, sign the SLA exhibit (DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/signon/?env=na1&acct=12345&gid=7392).
2) We will provision a dedicated onboarding JIRA and a post‑go‑live SLA acceptance review at 90 days.
3) If procurement requires the 99.5% permanent floor, request an executive call (I will loop in SVP Sales and VP Product).

Please review and let me know if procurement can accept the 99.8% phased floor. If yes, I’ll issue the DocuSign and we’ll schedule onboarding.

Thanks for working through this — appreciate the pragmatic approach.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (503) 555-0122

Attachments: redwood-counterproposal-sla-redline.docx
